svg.data-cooling: hot-swappable redundant fan modules in one field-replaceable tray
svg.data-software: ONIE installer pre-loaded; Open Network Linux (ONL) compatible
svg.data-timing: IEEE1588v2 and SyncE in hardware; PRTC ITU-T G.8272; integrated GNSS receiver
svg.data-stacking: two units; 2 of 3 QSFP28 for data, 1 RJ-45 for sync, 1 RJ-45 for control
svg.data-optics-qsfp28: 1x 40/100 GbE, 4x 10/25 GbE or 2x 50 GbE per port; DAC to 2 m and AOC to 30 m when stacking
svg.data-optics-sfp28: 25 GbE, 10 GbE or 1 GbE per port
svg.data-mgmt-ports: 1x RJ-45 1000BASE-T management, 1x RJ-45 serial console, 1x USB storage

This is the variant the datasheet's front elevation draws, and the quick start ships four ring lugs with it.","kind":"orderable","part-numbers":{"7315-27X-O-48X-S":{"part":"F0PZZ5627004A"}}}},"description":"20x 10G SFP+, 4x 25G SFP28 and 3x 100G QSFP28 cell site router, sold as the CSR310, Broadcom BCM88470 Qumran-AX with an Intel Atom C3508 and a Stratum 3E OCXO. An integrated GNSS receiver behind an SMA antenna input, six RJ-45s carrying stacking, timing and management, and two of the QSFP28s usable for stacking a second unit. Everything is on the front, including both hot-swappable supplies and the fan tray; side-to-side airflow.","format":1,"gaps":[{"reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["rear","top","bottom","left","right"],"wanted":"A figure of any face but the front. Neither document draws one, and on THIS device that is a smaller hole than usual: the datasheet's own \"All ports and PSUs are accessible at the front\" means the rear carries no user-facing hardware but the grounding point. The quick start's step 3 pictures that point twice, once on the rear panel and once on the side, as a two-hole lug with the earth symbol beside it - enough to know it exists on both, not enough to place either, so neither is placed. The SIDE panels carry the intake and exhaust on a side-to-side box and are drawn nowhere.","what":"rear-elevation"},{"reason":"needs-photo","scope":["front"],"wanted":"What the component at 239.8-260.8 is. It is 21.0 x 3.8 in the silkscreen band between the SFP+ numerals and the AS7315-27X model text, and it reads as eight cells with the outer two red and the inner six pale. Neither document mentions it: the fourteen callouts do not point at it, the specification lists no display and no switches, and the quick start's step 5 figure - which is otherwise the most legible thing in the corpus - is cropped just short of it. A stack-identity display would fit the device, which stacks two units and has a STACK-SYNC and a STACK-CTRL port; so would a DIP bank. It is drawn as a plain bezel with no claim about which, and `common/seven-segment-dual@1` was NOT used, because reaching for a part whose name asserts what the thing is would be the guess this gap exists to avoid.","what":"stack-id-indicator"},{"reason":"needs-photo","scope":["front"],"wanted":"The module letters on the two-high QSFP28 block at 322.5-342.5. The quick start names M0 (the single 100G cage) and M1 (the SFP28 group) outright, and the datasheet elevation carries a `M? 100GBASE-R` label over this block that does not resolve at 8.15 px/mm - it could be M2 or M3, and the block holds two ports whose own numbering is unread. They are modelled as `stack-0` and `stack-1` from the datasheet's callout 11, \"2 x 100G QSFP28 stacking ports\", which is a function rather than a name.","what":"stacking-qsfp-labels"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["front"],"wanted":"What the six lamps in the stacking block's bezel do. Their positions are measured - 325.1, 327.5, 330.4, 334.3, 337.5, 339.7 - and two of the six are visibly larger than the other four, which usually means a port lamp beside a set of lane lamps. Nothing in either document says. Four lane lamps and two port lamps is the shape the AGR110 uses, but that is a pattern, not a reading, so the six are placed and left unassigned.","what":"stacking-block-lamps"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["front"],"wanted":"How many fans are in the tray. The datasheet says \"Hot swappable redundant fan modules\" - plural, inside one tray - and the FRU table sells exactly one \"Fan Tray Spare Part\", FAN-1U-1x1J-S. The elevation shows a closed tray with no grille and no seams. So the tray is one module with no nested bays and the redundancy is stated in attrs without a count, rather than a number being invented to fill the field.","what":"fan-count"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["front"],"wanted":"A wattage for either supply. The datasheet's \"Power Capacity: 300 W (maximum)\" and the quick start's \"193 Watts maximum\" are both the CHASSIS's - one a capacity, one a consumption - and neither is an output rating for a module. Input ranges are published for both variants and are carried on the parts; the output is not, so L27 stands on both and the hole stays visible.","what":"psu-output-rating"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["front"],"wanted":"An LED table. Neither document has one. Six system lamps are named on the faceplate - LOC, DIAG, PSU1, PSU2, FAN, ALRM - and the quick start states one colour for four of them: \"After power on, the PSU1/PSU2, DIAG, ALRM, and FAN LEDs should all be on green.\" That is more than the CSR200 gives and still not a vocabulary, so every lamp carries `off` and one green `on`.","what":"led-vocabularies"}],"groups":{"fans":{"attrs":{"redundancy-note":"hot-swappable redundant fan modules in one field-replaceable tray. See the `fan-count` gap."},"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"leds":{"index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the management cluster - the 1000BASE-T RJ-45, the RS-232 console, the USB-A storage port and the Reset button.","role":"management","term":"Port"},"port-leds":{"index-origin":0,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"psus":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"two load-sharing hot-swappable supplies, AC or -48 VDC"},"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"qsfp28":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp28","speed":"100g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"sfp-plus":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp-plus","speed":"10g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"sfp28":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp28","speed":"25g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"stacking":{"index-origin":0,"mixed":"the stacking cluster - two of the three 100G QSFP28 cages carry the data path between a pair of CSR310s, and the STACK-CTRL RJ-45 carries the \"1 x 1 GbE from CPU (control signal)\" the datasheet lists beside them. Two media, one job. The datasheet counts the QSFP28s in its port total and names them separately in callout 11; both are true, and this group is how a consumer finds the ones that are spoken for. STACK-SYNC IS NOT IN HERE. The datasheet lists it separately as \"1 x RJ-45 for sync signals\", and a sync signal is not Ethernet: leaving it in a `traffic` group typed it as a gigabit interface AND as a timing port, and it was exported twice under one name. It sits in `timing` with the BITS and PPS/ToD jacks, which is what it carries.","role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"timing":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the synchronisation cluster - a BITS RJ-45, a PPS/ToD RJ-45, the STACK-SYNC RJ-45 and the SMA antenna input of the integrated GNSS receiver. No front-to-back part number is listed and none is assumed."},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - \"Dimensions (WxDxH): 440 x 300 x 44 mm (17.32 x 11.81 x 1.73 in)\" and \"Weight 5.35 kg (11.79 lb), with two installed PSUs\". The quick start's hardware specification restates both to the digit, so the two agree and there is nothing to record as a disagreement. 440 is the body width: the datasheet's own \"Can be mounted in standard 19', 21', 23', and ETSI 600 mm racks\" makes the brackets an accessory outside it, and the quick start ships them as \"Rack Mounting Kit - 2 brackets and 8 screws\" with two hole patterns, for 300 mm and 280 mm deep racks."},"figure-choice":{"confidence":"measured","note":"Gate 1, and this is the best figure in the Edgecore corpus so far. Page 2 rendered at 600 dpi; panel found by row/column darkness at (615,2136)-(4199,2494), 3585 x 359 px, aspect 9.9861 against 10.0 for 440/44 - 0.14 PERCENT OUT. The CSR200's was 1.86 and the CSR180's 1.47. At that agreement the art is an orthographic elevation rather than a camera render, and x carries geometry directly at 8.1477 px/mm. IT IS ALSO THE LOWEST RESOLUTION: 8.15 px/mm against the CSR200's 9.63, because it is drawn smaller on the page. Truer and coarser at once, which is why the division of labour below exists - the datasheet says WHERE and the quick start says WHAT. The quick start's own elevations were rejected: page 3, 6 and 9 carry the same drawing at 5.05 px/mm and 6 to 9 percent of aspect error."},"gnss":{"confidence":"measured","note":"AN SMA, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, which the issue asked for explicitly. The connector reads 10.0 mm across on the elevation - common/sma-jack@1 is 9.5 across flats and common/smb-jack@1 is 7.0 - and the quick start's step 4a and step 7 figures both show a gold hex-nut bulkhead, which is an SMA and is not an SMB. Centred on 135.90, directly above the M0 cage on the same centreline."},"optical-blocks":{"confidence":"measured","note":"Every optical block is anchored on a MEASURED CENTRE and sized from the registry, and here the two agree far better than on the CSR180. The SFP+ group's outer edges read 179.03 and 321.17 - 142.14 across ten columns, or 14.214 each, against the registry's 14.25, a fifth of a percent. The SFP28 group reads 147.79 to 176.87, 14.54 a column over two columns. The RJ-45 block's internal walls read 347.0, 360.99 and 375.22, a 14.11 pitch against a registry 13.97. Origins are the block centres: 178.85, 148.08 and 347.00. Rows: the bezel between the two cage rows centres on 18.14 down a column, so the pair is placed to straddle it at the registry's 15.0 row pitch, putting the top row at 5.44."},"port-numbering":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"THREE INDEPENDENT NUMBER SPACES, WHICH IS WHY THE IDS ARE NOT `port-N` THROUGHOUT. The quick start's step 5 figure is flat, large and unambiguous: the single 100G cage is labelled `M0 100GBASE-R` and its port is numbered `0`; the four-port SFP28 group is bracketed `M1 1/10/25GBASE-R` and numbered `0 1 2 3`; and the twenty-port SFP+ group RESTARTS AT 0, running `0 1` through `18 19`. All three were read again off the datasheet elevation's own numerals and agree. So `m0-0`, `m1-0..m1-3` and `port-0..port-19` are three ranges that would collide if they shared a prefix, and the block `id-format` is what keeps them apart."},"psus-and-fans":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"REAL FIELD-REPLACEABLE UNITS WITH PART NUMBERS, unlike every other CSR in this library. The datasheet's own FRU table names CRXT-T0T12BS (DC PSU), SPAACTN-03BG (AC PSU) and FAN-1U-1x1J-S (fan tray), and the quick start adds that only CRXT-T0T12B will fit the DC bay. Two supply bays at 4.54 and 67.06 - a 62.52 pitch confirmed by the warning triangles printed on the modules, 62.6 apart - each 54.08 wide, with 8.4 mm of chassis between them. The fan tray runs 394.3 to the panel edge. THE ELEVATION SHOWS THE DC VARIANT. The AC module's face comes from the quick start's step 4a, which is legible for what is on it - a C14 inlet marked N, earth and L, the same handle and the same latch - and useless for where, so edgecore/csr310-psu-ac@1 borrows its envelope from the DC unit and says so."},"sources":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"Two documents, both staged and both docling-converted, MEASURED OFF THE PDF PAGES RATHER THAN THE CONVERTED FIGURES, and USED FOR DIFFERENT THINGS. csr310-datasheet carries the specification list, the ordering matrix, the field-replacement part numbers and the fourteen-callout front elevation on page 2 that every coordinate here is read from. csr310-qsg carries no figure worth measuring and is the source of nearly every NAME: its step 5, 6 and 7 illustrations are large, flat and legible where the elevation is 8.15 px/mm and is not."},"the-rj45-six":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"SIX RJ-45s IN ONE 2x3 BLOCK, AND THE QUICK START NAMES EVERY ONE. Its step 7 figure reads, top row left to right, STACK-SYNC / BITS / Console, and bottom row STACK-CTRL / PPS-ToD / Mgmt. Below them sit six lamps in three groups: a bracketed LINK and ACT under STACK-CTRL, an up-arrow BITS and a down-arrow PPS under the middle column, and a bracketed LINK and ACT under Mgmt. THE ARROWS ARE THE POINT. The middle column's two lamps serve BOTH of its jacks - the up-arrow one reports the BITS port above, the down-arrow one the PPS/ToD port below - which is the same convention the AGR110 uses on its uplinks and the thing that had to be left as a gap on the CSR180 because its art would not resolve it."}},"references":[{"sha256":"986dc816058d621dec5d08e6f0c2f807455c356c5acd4b501ec359cd3e52e5f9","title":"Edgecore CSR310 / AS7315-27X Cell Site Router Data Sheet"},{"sha256":"74cd15954d27b1ec3cfd5ec3707ae295f60063b7b44b32a008ff05013867ba8b","title":"Edgecore AS7315-27X Cell Site Gateway Quick Start Guide E112022-CS-R05"}],"version":"1.0.1","views":{"bottom":{"empty":"Not drawn by any staged source.
